ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 2015 (as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 and Ley 75 de 2019); Decreto Ejecutivo 363 de 2015; Decreto Ejecutivo 213 de 2019; Directivas del Registro Publico on the Registro Unico de Beneficiarios Finales (statutory UBO filing threshold of 10% direct or indirect ownership or control); Ley 32 de 1927 (Sociedades Anonimas); Codigo de Comercio; FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 24 and 25; regulatory guidelines of the Intendencia de Supervision y Regulacion de Sujetos No Financieros (INL) and the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the proposed Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos) for notarial execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notario Publico del Circuito de Panama or competent foreign notary for the draft

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder) appointing the resident agent and incorporating counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian notary or foreign notary in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of identity of each director, officer, shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Country-of-origin notary, competent civil registrar, or consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; accompanied by enhanced KYC certificates

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or equivalent registry certificate for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs and signatories against the UAF Lista de Personas Designadas, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List and Panamanian domestic designations; enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs under FATF Recommendation 12 and Ley 23 de 2015 Article 27; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification; adverse media and negative news checks; prohibition of bearer-share use unless the certificates are immobilized in the custody of a licensed Panamanian financial intermediary; retention of AML/CFT records for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Plataforma de Servicios en Linea (Sistema de Reserva y Certificacion de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Spanish or a foreign language but must be transliterated into Latin script. The corporate name must end with 'Sociedad Anonima', 'S.A.', or an accepted English equivalent clearly denoting a corporation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must not imply a legal form inconsistent with the Sociedad Anonima status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a Recurso de Reconsideracion with the Direccion General del Registro Publico within five business days under Ley 38 de 2000, attaching evidence of prior use, common-law trademark rights, or equivalence with the rejected name; the registry must resolve within ten business days. A clerical re-application with up to three alternative names may be submitted immediately. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within thirty business days. No additional government fee applies to the first administrative reconsideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office using the licensed resident agent's address satisfies the minimum statutory registered-office requirement for incorporation. However, for an M&A advisory boutique claiming commercial substance in Panama, the INL and DGI may expect locally verifiable decision-making, physical or commercially genuine presence, availability of books and records, and senior staff. Sole reliance on a virtual office creates a heightened substance-inspection and audit trigger.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium: approximately 35% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection or documentary data request within the first fiscal year, based on INL risk-based supervision of newly registered non-financial subjects and DGI territorial-substance verification programs.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry incorporation fee scale based on authorized capital, US$10,000 authorized capital reference

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent first-annual fee including registered office address services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Panama DNFBP risk-tier enhanced due-diligence packages

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporations Law on Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Law 5 of 2001 and Law 49 of 2002; Public Registry Regulations (Acuerdo No. 4 of 2003); Decree Law 2 of 2011 for AML obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama), Departamento de Personas Jurídicas (Office of Legal Persons).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución / Pacto Social (Articles of Incorporation executed as a public deed before a licensed Panamanian Notary Public and subsequently inscribed in the Public Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under Law 32 of 1927; the authorized and subscribed capital is freely determined in the Escritura Pública, with at least one share issued. No statutory escrow, bank deposit, or capital verification certificate is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Directors of [Company], S.A., assembled this [day] of [month], 2025, that: 1. Subscription. The subscription of the Company's authorized share capital by the founding shareholders is approved, and the issuance and allocation of shares are ratified. 2. Registered Office. The registered office located at [property/building, floor, district, Panama] is adopted as the Company's statutory seat, as recorded with the Public Registry of Panama, for governance and service of process. 3. Officers. [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as President, Treasurer, and Secretary, respectively, holding the powers set out in the Articles of Incorporation. 4. Authorization. Officers are authorized to execute banking forms, engage auditors, and register the Company with the Municipality, DGI, CSS, MITRADEL, and other competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Corporate Name Reservation System (Servicios en Línea) or Customer Service Window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a formal name-search application to verify availability of the proposed S.A. name. Once cleared, request a formal Reserva de Nombre, which grants an exclusive renewable right for a statutory period (typically 30 days). Retain the issued reservation certificate for filing with the notary.
required_dossiers: Completed name search application form (Formulario de Búsqueda)
Three alternative proposed corporate names in descending preference
Copy of the applicant's national ID or passport
Payment of official search and reservation fee (approx. USD 10–20)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or confusion, promptly submit a revised set of names or file a written reconsideration request with the Registro Público name-review committee; the reservation fee may be reapplied to new names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública of the Notarial Circuit of Panama (Notario autorizado, Circuito de Panamá).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating shareholders (or their attorney-in-fact) execute the Escritura Pública de Constitución, including the corporate name, precise M&A advisory purpose clause, authorized capital structure, board composition, governance provisions, registered office address, and duration. Signature is completed before the notary, who verifies identity and capacity. For foreign incorporators, certified passports and duly legalized powers of attorney are required.
required_dossiers: Draft Escritura Pública de Constitución / Pacto Social
Valid corporate name reservation certificate
Certified passport copies of all subscribers or incorporating shareholders
Notarized power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of any subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects or missing documentary requisites, the deed is corrected and re-executed before the same notary; alternatively, a supplementary correction deed (acta de modificación) is executed to cure non-material errors without invalidating the original deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Company in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Personas Jurídicas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Escritura Pública together with the applicable inscription fee and stamp duties for registration. The Registrar issues the Ficha de Sociedad / Certificado de Inscripción, which is conclusive evidence of legal existence. After inscription, obtain certified copies of the Ficha and the recorded deed for use before tax, municipal, and banking authorities.
required_dossiers: Notarized copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Official inscription fee payment of approximately USD 250
Payment of legal-grade stamp duties (papel sellado)
Certified power of attorney and corporate resolutions, if a foreign entity is a subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a qualification defect, file a corrective brief and supplementary documents within the statutory period; in case of rejection, the incorporators may appeal the decision (recurso de apelación) before the higher legal authority of the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Identification (RUC) Registration with the DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A. in the RUC system to obtain the corporate taxpayer identification number and tax obligations profile. File the RUC application with the DGI, indicating the office-based professional services activity (ISIC 7020 – management consulting / M&A advisory), territorial-source fiscal regime, and the legal representative's details. The resulting RUC certificate is required for banking, municipal licensing, and importing records.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificate of Inscription (Ficha) from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Legal representative's ID or passport and proof of Panamanian fiscal domicile
Completed RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the application due to inconsistent data or missing documents, submit the corrected information in person and designate a fiscal-domicile representative if the RUC reflects deficiencies; alternatively, request an administrative rectification of the RUC record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá – Dirección de Avisos de Operación, Tesorería Municipal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación (municipal commercial operating notice/license) before commencing business in Panama City, classifying the activity as 'servicios profesionales y técnicas' (professional and technical services). Pay the municipal fee, which is assessed based on the company's estimated paid-in capital and gross revenue projections. The license is valid until the annual renewal date and is a precondition for opening a physical office.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación application form of the Municipality of Panama
RUC certificate issued by the DGI
Certified Ficha de Registro Público
Fire safety compliance certificate for the intended office premises
Lease agreement or certificate of ownership of the office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects or suspends the application, pay the assessed differential fee or submit the missing documents within the municipal deadline; an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Mayor's Office if the license is denied on substantive grounds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the CSS, MITRADEL, and UAF (Post-Incorporation Mandatory Registrations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) – Employers Registry; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); and Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the S.A. as an employer with the CSS for social security contributions; file the establishment registration and employee contracts with MITRADEL for labor compliance; and, because the firm acts as a Designated Non-Financial Business or Profession (DNFBP) under Law 2 of 2011, file the AML registration with the UAF, appoint a Compliance Officer, and implement the AML/CFT manual appropriate for Medium-Risk Enhanced M&A advisory transactions.
required_dossiers: CSS employer registration forms and payroll data
Standard employment contract templates for MITRADEL
MITRADEL business establishment registration form
UAF DNFBP registration file with AML/CFT compliance manual, risk assessment, and Compliance Officer designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CSS and MITRADEL observations are cured by amending payroll forms or employment contracts and resubmitting electronically; UAF deficiencies require a revised compliance manual and reappointment of the compliance officer, with an administrative reconsideration available before the UAF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for general commercial registry matters; Alcaldía de Panamá, Dirección de Avisos de Operación for the operational business license; Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV) only where the M&A advisory activity involves public securities offerings or regulated investment advice under Decree Law 1 of 8 July 1999.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice / Commercial License) issued by the Municipality of Panama, supplemented, if applicable, by registration with the SMV as a Financial Adviser (Asesor de Inversiones) when the firm provides securities-related advice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental (National Environmental Assessment Directorate).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Low Environmental Impact (Registro de Impacto Ambiental / Registration only). A full Environmental Impact Assessment is expressly not required for an office-based M&A advisory services firm with no industrial or physical processing activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater must comply with the discharge limits of IDAAN (Instituto de Acueductos y Alcantarillados Nacionales) and MiAMBIENTE's water-quality rules; no significant VOC or particulate emissions are generated by an office operation, but any HVAC and emergency generator must meet permitted noise and combustion standards; solid waste, including e-waste and confidential paper records, must be segregated and disposed of through municipal or licensed private collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Seguridad, Prevención y Protección contra Incendios) issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá after inspection of the office premises; structural and occupancy clearance from the Municipality of Panama (Dirección de Obras y Construcciones) validating the building load and occupational capacity; and workplace health & safety registration with MITRADEL, including first-aid, emergency-exit, and ergonomic compliance for the professional advisory staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama; official e-portal: Sede Electrónica (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) by registered public deed (escritura pública) at the Registro Público and appoint a resident agent (abogado idóneo). Step 2: Secure the municipal Aviso de Operación at the Alcaldía de Panamá for the business address. Step 3: Obtain DGI Sede Electrónica access (TAN account), file the RUC inscription form, and submit the notarized deed, board resolution appointing the legal representative, passports/power of attorney for non-resident officers, and proof of local address. Step 4: Receive the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) certificate, fiscal classification, and electronic signature/token. Step 5: Where the boutique concludes contracts locally or hires Panamanian staff, also register with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and the municipality; unless excluded, a service exporter registration with DGI/MICI should be requested to substantiate territorial sourcing of cross-border fees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — the Panamanian S.A. is a separate legal entity taxed at the corporate level under the Impuesto sobre la Renta (ISR) only on Panamanian-source income; foreign-source M&A advisory income falls outside the Panamanian tax net, and dividends paid to non-resident shareholders are exempt from Panamanian withholding tax. No pass-through status is recognized for domestic tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not implement U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections. Available statutory elections: (i) Sociedad de Inversión (Investment Holding Company) election under Law 32 of 2011, covering foreign-source dividends, interest and capital gains; (ii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) licence under Law 41 of 2007, granting reduced income and indirect tax benefits for regional service hubs (subject to MICI criteria); (iii) small taxpayer simplified regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) under Law 318 of 2022 where annual gross income does not exceed PAB/USD 20,000.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama's VAT on goods transfers and services, including professional M&A advisory fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold: every taxable person supplying professional services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable transaction. A small taxpayer alternative applies only where annual gross turnover is PAB/USD 20,000 or less, in which case the DGI permits a fixed simplified payment instead of full monthly declarations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all active taxpayers: invoices must be generated through DGI-certified billing software connected to the Sede Electrónica e-invoicing module (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica), transmitted electronically (API/web-services) with a fiscal security code (Código de Seguridad Fiscal) and QR; the DGI validates and returns an acceptance token in near-real-time. Export invoices (facturas de exportación) are separate e-document types referencing the customs or service-export registration. Paper-only invoicing is invalid except under transitional DGI regulations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies to (i) goods physically exported under Panama Customs procedures and (ii) services rendered to non-resident clients provided the benefit/economic use occurs outside Panama — which includes cross-border M&A advisory, merger structuring, due diligence and success-fee brokerage services performed for foreign acquirers or targets. Zero-rating is denied where the services are effectively exploited, or the direct beneficiary is resident, in Panama.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera — DUA, processed through SIGA)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (Conocimiento de Embarque / Guía Aérea) for goods-based exports
Commercial invoice and signed M&A advisory agreement identifying the non-resident counterparty and the offshore use of the service
Certificado de exportador de servicios / service-export certificate issued by DGI/MICI for cross-border advisory revenue
Inward Remittance Certificate from the receiving Panamanian bank evidencing timely collection of the foreign-currency fee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit zero-rating files within the statutory prescription window (typically 3–5 years). Missing or inconsistent substantiation triggers retroactive assessment of the 7% ITBMS, monthly moratory interest, and fines: 10%–50% for documentary infractions and up to 100%–200% of the omitted tax for fraudulent invoices or simulated exports, plus criminal liability (fines and imprisonment) for falsified customs/export certificates. The taxpayer may also be removed from the e-invoicing and exporter registers, suspending the right to zero-rate future invoices.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank; monetary supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), which supervises all banking activities. The U.S. dollar serves as the sole legal tender and fiscal currency under the Monetary Agreement with the United States (1904), so there is no domestic monetary issuance authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Panamanian balboa is a nominal unit of account with no physical currency; only U.S. dollar banknotes circulate. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible without exchange control restrictions. No central bank approval is required for repatriation of capital, dividends, or profits. Banks may impose their own internal documentation requirements for large remittances under AML/CFT obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no surrender requirements, no mandatory conversion timelines, and no legal quota for foreign currency earnings generated by Panamanian entities. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency, freely transferred, or offset against imports and trade settlements. Panama's territorial tax system taxes only income derived from Panama-sourced operations, and the tax authorities do not impose foreign exchange conversion or repatriation conditions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium–Restricted. Panama does not recognise a standalone 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) licence in the EU/UK sense. Law 23 of 2021 introduced a fintech sandbox and permits digital banking and 'technological financial innovation' activities, but a full banking or specialised licence is needed to hold client funds. Offshore EMIs without a local banking licence cannot maintain accounts directly, but can operate as white-label payment facilitators through local banks or through authorised 'Interbank National Payment Services' under SBP regulations. The SBP requires local presence and a full compliance infrastructure for any entity receiving deposits or executing payments. Thus, cross-border EMIs should partner with a tier-1 Panamanian bank rather than attempt direct account access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required once for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and in-person authorised signatories of the Sociedad Anónima when opening a corporate account at most Panamanian banks. Remote opening is permitted only in rare, lower-risk cases and only when the bank conducts a videoconference interview, receives notarised and certified corporate documents (Apostilled under the Hague Convention), and obtains certified copies of passports from a recognised local consulate or subscribing notary. For a medium-risk M&A advisory boutique, banks will almost always demand at least one in-person appearance by the compliance officer, a senior director, or the UBO before activating the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or client resides in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction or non-cooperative territory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial ownership documentation, source of wealth statement, professional or bank reference letters from a FATF-compliant institution, audited corporate financials, and documentary proof of the underlying cross-border transaction value chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client is a politically exposed person (PEP) or has PEP-related counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration forms, source of funds analysis, transaction-specific purpose letters, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring attestation from the advisory firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of layered corporate vehicles (special purpose entities, foundations) that obscure ultimate ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry chain from Panama's RFM (Registro Federal de Multas) or Public Registry, notarised trust/foundation declarations, beneficial ownership certificates, and a clear economic substance rationale tied to the M&A mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high upfront retainer or success fee to be received without prior business track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engagement letter, valuation or advisory report, copy of the signed transaction term sheet, bank statements of the source payer, and audited financial statements of the client's operating entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border or multi-currency transactions involving jurisdictions with possible sanctions implications
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from at least one commercial tool (e.g., OFAC, UNSC, EU lists), export/import control certificates, trade documents, and a robust corporate compliance manual binding the advisory firm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Panamanian advisory boutique is typically routed via U.S. dollar wire transfers (SWIFT MT103) from the parent entity or non-resident shareholder. No exchange-control approval is needed. Banks require the remitter to include a clear payment reference such as 'Capital Contribution', 'Additional Paid-in Capital', or 'Retained Earnings Distribution', and require the local entity to submit a Certificate of Due Incorporation, corporate resolutions, and a sworn statement of source of funds. Larger injections may require the bank's AML committee to review the economic substance and the underlying acquisition mandate. If the capital is injected as a loan, a loan agreement with commercial terms and signature legalisation is mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement and success-fee disbursements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 (serial/cover payments) for wire transfers and commercial letters of credit for documentary transactions. For M&A advisory fees, SWIFT MT103 with appropriate purpose codes (e.g., service fee, IP royalty, professional fees) and supporting invoice/engagement letter are required. There are no restrictions on outbound transfers, but the bank must complete a transaction form covering the beneficiary, purpose, and source of funds. Large outbound payments may trigger enhanced due diligence and potential notification to the SBP under the AML threshold for cash or suspicious transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated plain-vanilla forward contracts with local banks (though not needed for USD-based settlements), typically 30–90 days tenor.
Cross-currency NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) against USD for exposure to non-convertible currencies (e.g., acquired subsidiaries in certain Latin American jurisdictions).

FX swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency swaps) for temporary rebalancing of receivables in foreign currencies, executed via international banks with a local banking branch or through a repurchase counterparty.
Interest-rate swaps (if a debt facility is leveraged) - permissible as a treasury hedge when linked to the funding structure.
Currency options (European-style) for conversion of foreign transaction proceeds into USD without balance-sheet exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax / annuity – Tasa Única de Personas Jurídicas (Anualidad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; evidence lodged with the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year annuity; due no later than July 31 of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incremental late penalty of USD 100 if paid after July 31 and before October 31; USD 200 penalty plus 10% annual interest after October 31. Failure for five consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off/suspension of the corporate record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income-tax declaration – Declaración Anual de Renta, Formulario 150 (territorial basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year = calendar year; filing due by June 30 of the following year. A nil/zero return is required where no Panama-source income is generated.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax liability, plus monthly interest; persistent default freezes tax-clearance certificates and can trigger closure orders and loss of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation and AML record update for AML-regulated non-financial M&A advisory entities (UBO annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent and correspondent files; Public Registry of Panama (UBO section) and Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for AML-regulated subjects
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after the incorporation anniversary (or per registry calendar schedule); within 15 business days after any share-transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 50,000 for false, stale, or omitted UBO disclosure; potential suspension of the regulated-entity license and rejection of registry filings until corrected.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if: (i) the entity holds an SMV/UAF-regulated M&A advisory or financial-services license; (ii) DGI classifies it as a “gran contribuyente”; or (iii) it exceeds Panama’s local-GAAP audit threshold (commonly around USD 1,000,000 in annual gross receipts or USD 500,000 in total assets). A private offshore S.A. without those features has no statutory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama-licensed financial and securities entities apply IFRS (NIIF); private commercial companies may apply IFRS for SMEs or Panamanian GAAP under the Commercial Code.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panama's AML/UBO framework (Ley 23 de 2015 and complementary regulations), every S.A. must maintain accurate beneficial-owner identification. The registered agent must obtain annual confirmation irrespective of ownership changes; any share transfer requires updated UBO confirmation within 15 business days. Non-compliance produces fines, registry filing blocks, and license consequences for regulated advisory entities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Oficiales)
Register of Share Transfers (Registro de Transferencias)
Minute Book of Board and Shareholders (Libro de Actas)
AML/UBO due-diligence file maintained by the resident agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – USD 16,000 per issue for a licensed M&A advisory S.A.; not incurred if no audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% under the general ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) regime on net taxable income; territorial sourcing applies, so only Panamanian-source M&A advisory success fees and retainers are within the headline rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general preferential deduction applies to a standard S.A. under ISIC 7020; the territorial system excludes foreign-source success fees where the engagement is performed entirely abroad; a qualifying Multinational Headquarters (SEM) company under Law 41 of 2007 may obtain a reduced 10% ISR rate on Panamanian-source income and 0% on foreign-source income, subject to substance, minimum local operating expenditures and annual reporting; large taxpayers with net taxable income above USD 1,500,000 are additionally subject to the CAIR supplementary calculation mechanism (effective combined loading approximating the 25% headline).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 200 - Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta; filed electronically through the DGI E-Tax 2.0 portal (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa) using the RUC-based user authentication of the appointed legal representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; complemented by monthly Pago Directo advance payments within the same fiscal year, all settled and reconciled in the annual Form 200.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before March 15 of the calendar year following the close of the fiscal year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 90 days of fiscal-year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The S.A.'s 12-digit tax identification number; must be obtained before any filing and kept active with the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned S.A. must maintain a Panamanian legal representative holding a current taxpayer PIN; the representative must authenticate every e-filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beginning and ending dates of the fiscal year (standard: January 1 to December 31).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Changes to the fiscal year require prior DGI notification and must be reflected in the company minutes for non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Ingresos Gravables de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue from M&A advisory, diligence, retainer and success-fee engagements where the service is economically performed in Panama or used in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the Panamanian sourcing engagement-by-engagement; do not route Panamanian-sourced fees directly to an offshore holding company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Ingresos Exentos y de Fuente Extranjera
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source success fees (services wholly rendered abroad) and exempt Panamanian-source income; declared for information only under territoriality.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain time sheets, client location evidence and execution files showing the engagement was performed outside Panama to support the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, office rent, data and market-research costs, professional fees and other expenses supported by valid invoices and bank transfers; deductions require that corresponding WHT was paid on local invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident suppliers' invoices for royalties or technical assistance are deductible only if the 12.5% WHT advance was actually withheld and remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from the preceding five fiscal years applied against current net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward schedules must reconcile with prior-year accepted returns; the DGI may reject carry-forwards if the underlying returns were filed late.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Impuesto a Pagar antes de Créditos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISR computed at 25% on net taxable income; CAIR-adjusted large taxpayers reflect the required supplementary calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the advance payments system does not convert a withholding obligation into an apparent additional corporate tax burden.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Créditos y Saldo a Pagar o a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for monthly Pago Directo advances and WHT suffered on income; result is the final balance payable with the return or the refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not claim corporate tax credits personally; overpaid credits remain at the S.A. level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late payment generates a 1% per-month surcharge (maximum 50% of the unpaid tax) plus default interest; a minimum administrative fine of USD 500 applies to a missing or materially defective return; intentional under-declaration is criminal tax evasion with 2 to 5 years' imprisonment and fines of USD 20,000 to USD 200,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 850 - Declaración de Transacciones con Partes Relacionadas; filed electronically in the DGI E-Tax 2.0 portal as an accompanying statement to Form 200.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, coordinated with the corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as Form 200: March 15 for calendar-year taxpayers; within 90 days of fiscal-year close for off-calendar years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section A - Identificación de la Parte Relacionada
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, jurisdiction, tax identification and relationship of each related foreign counterparty (parent, subsidiaries, shareholder holding companies).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent groups must annually complete a related-party questionnaire to permit accurate disclosure of intra-group fee sharing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B - Tipos y Montos de Transacciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border transactions exceeding USD 1,000,000: management fees, success-fee splits, loans, interest, royalties and IP transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: M&A boutiques commonly enter international fee-split and referral arrangements; all must be disclosed even if economically immaterial to the group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C - Método de Precios de Transferencia Aplicado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the arm's length method applied (CUP, Resale, Cost Plus, TNMM or Profit Split) and the selected tested party.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Method selection requires contemporaneous benchmark comparables; do not adopt a method solely because the non-resident parent uses it in its own filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary transfer pricing adjustments made by the taxpayer to bring the tax base to arm's length before the DGI review.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A voluntary adjustment reduces the 50% fraud surcharge to the standard rate and demonstrates cooperative compliance; however it also reveals the original under-declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 850 triggers an administrative penalty of USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 plus re-assessment of cross-border transactions at arm's length with a 25% surcharge on the under-declared tax and 1% per-month default interest.
